risks.note: Availability of suitable quality granite blocks is critical to product quality and production continuity; changes in quarrying activity, availability of commercially viable blocks, and higher extraction/transportation costs can affect raw material availability and cost structures.
risks.risk: Availability and cost of raw material

risks.note: Mining and processing activities are subject to statutory, environmental and regulatory requirements; changes in regulations, restrictions on mining, or approval delays may affect raw material availability and operating timelines.

The industry depends on an efficient transportation and shipping network, particularly for exports; freight rate fluctuations, container availability, port congestion and shipping disruptions can raise costs and affect delivery schedules.

Demand for natural stone is closely linked to construction, housing and renovation activity in major export markets; slowdowns, tariff/trade-policy changes, geopolitical developments or shifts in customer spending can affect export volumes and realisations.
Significant competition from domestic producers and international suppliers, combined with input cost fluctuations, can pressure selling prices and margins.

As an export-oriented business, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange rate movements as well as fluctuations in fuel, power, freight and other input costs, which can impact operating costs and profitability if not adequately managed.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange and input cost fluctuations

risks.note: Customer preferences in construction and interiors continue to evolve with increasing choices across natural and engineered surfaces, requiring the Company to maintain product relevance, quality and design variety to retain market position.
